scope: Standalone prepared-load consumer. No production IQ/ROB/data-port integration, store write path, cache, LSQ, forwarding, architectural retirement or full-core acceptance. Uses the existing memory protocol and shared verification runner. No physical timing claim.
launch: launch_i is an accepted prepared load descriptor, qualified by ready_o. Preserve full 13-bit ROB identity. Caller retains instruction/PC/operand metadata for later completion. Legal sizes/signs are LB/LH/LW/LBU/LHU. Nonfault descriptors already passed alignment and PMA checks in load_store_prepare; stores are routed elsewhere. Fault descriptors carry cause 4 or 5 and trap_value=address and complete locally without a request. There is no same-cycle consume/refill.
permission: A held nonfault descriptor waits for issue_allowed_i, which the future memory-order owner must qualify using all older-store hazards, forwarding and drain rules. Head-only or uncached reads additionally require head_valid_i and exact head_id_i. No cached/idempotent eligibility flag grants bus permission by itself. Once offered, permissions no longer withdraw a request. All write fields are zero.
data: Cached requests read the containing 32-byte aligned line; uncached requests carry the exact byte address and size. Uncached return data occupies the containing aligned 32-bit word lanes, matching the existing single-lane protocol adapter, with all unrequested lanes zero. Load results select little-endian bytes and sign/zero extend. Access-fault responses yield cause 5, trap_value=effective address and zero data. Held result metadata is immutable; invalid result and request payloads are zero.
cancel: kill_i is externally qualified against owner_id_o, not a blanket flush. Before offering, any descriptor may be canceled. Offered/accepted cacheable idempotent reads retain request/ID ownership and drain their response without completion, including access faults and kill/response collisions. MMIO reads cannot be canceled after offering through successful result consumption; irrevocable_o identifies that interval. Caller must defer recovery until that head operation completes. Faulted MMIO results can be canceled. Reset overrides ownership only under the target reset contract.
protocol: One request at a time, minimum response latency one cycle, no response-cycle launch/turnover. Four-bit transaction IDs advance only on well-formed response handshakes, including discarded reads. Wrong IDs, unsolicited/same-cycle/duplicate responses, wrong payload class, nonzero unrequested uncached lanes, nonzero fault payloads and protocol/reserved statuses set sticky fatal_o on the next edge, even for canceled traffic. Fatal suppresses channels until reset. busy_o includes descriptors, offered/accepted reads and held results; fatal_o must separately block global drain and retirement. Reset requires the target to suppress pre-reset responses.
